A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TetSphere Splatting. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching retained content across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original reconstruction experiments, computational-cost measurements, generation examples and an energy-coefficient analysis in Sections 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds inverse-rendering comparisons, representation-resolution ablations and a tetrahedron-inversion experiment in Appendices A, B and D.

M1.justification: The tetrahedral primitives, deformation objective, regularization, silhouette-based initialization and texture optimization remain unchanged. Appendix I newly explains surface extraction and union; it does not establish a revised procedure.

E1.justification: The reconstruction and image/text-to-3D tasks retain their closed-surface, open-surface and slender-object coverage. The revised auxiliary-object count stays within that coverage. The new ablations and shrinking-sphere example examine the existing deformation procedure rather than establishing a new task or population.

E2.justification: v4 adds NeuS and VolSDF to the multi-view comparison in Table 1. New Table 4 and Figure 8 evaluate Nicolet et al. (2021) and Palfinger (2022), substantially extending comparison to single-primitive inverse-rendering approaches. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs sweep five TetSphere counts per selected shape, cross four average counts with five tetrahedral resolutions, and compare regularization enabled versus disabled. Table 5 adds triangle-count reporting. Separately, Section 5.2 revises three auxiliary models from Objaverse/Adobe Stock to two from Objaverse; this reported setting change does not establish benchmark reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained energy-coefficient study, Appendix B tests primitive-count sensitivity and the trade-off between primitive count and tetrahedra per primitive. Appendix D tests whether volumetric regularization prevents inversion. Appendix A adds qualitative analysis of inverse-rendering failures on complex topology.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. The new ablation curves provide point results without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Previously reported numerical entries remain unchanged, but v4 adds substantial results. Table 4 reports Chamfer distances of 0.0213, 0.0191 and 0.0184 for Nicolet, Palfinger and TetSphere respectively, while explicitly reporting ties on MR and CC Diff. Other additions include NeuS/VolSDF scores, triangle counts, count-resolution trends and inversion outcomes.

T1.justification: The optimization equations, deformation-gradient derivation, initialization formulation and paracompactness argument are retained. Appendix C supplies formulas for existing standard evaluation metrics; Appendix L adds qualitative regularization rationale. Neither introduces a new theorem, proof or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain high-quality geometry through deformable tetrahedral primitives, superior mesh quality with competitive reconstruction accuracy, and applicability to image/text-to-3D generation. Added evidence supports these retained claims without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: Beyond v3's topology-preservation caveat, v4 clarifies that overlapping pieces do not form a globally consistent tetrahedral mesh and that unions may lose manifoldness. Appendices A, B and L add substantive explanations of comparator failures, primitive-count trade-offs and regularization in unobserved regions.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code repository link, surface-extraction and union details, explicit metric formulas, and the primary dress/sorter TetSphere counts of 323/127. These are disclosures rather than demonstrated implementation changes. The sentence identifying generation-image and text-prompt provenance is removed from Section 5.4.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A substantially expand positioning against single-primitive inverse rendering, explaining differences in remeshing, topology and volumetric regularization. v4 also discusses Mosaic SDF and adds geometry-processing precedents in Appendix L, while removing several earlier representation and novel-view-generation references.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. Changes include localized related-work and conclusion rewrites, additional explanatory appendix sections, fuller captions, updated affiliations and conference headers, and corresponding cross-reference adjustments.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 4, Figures 8–10 and the inversion illustration in Appendix D, creating substantial new comparative and analytical displays. Table 1 gains comparator rows, and old Table 4 becomes Table 5 with a triangle-count row. Original appendix Figures 8–10 are retained as Figures 11–13 with expanded captions.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens validation of the central representation: comparisons with closely related inverse-rendering methods and controlled primitive-count, resolution and inversion studies address important gaps in v3. Explicit metric definitions, surface-union details and stronger limitations improve transparency. The unexplained sample-composition revision alongside unchanged legacy aggregates limits cross-version interpretation, but the added validation and clearer applicability boundaries provide substantial overall gains.
